mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES at t-0w indicates commuters are returning to shared destinations; that transfer should lift discretionary footfall into retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior four-week mean even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain above their t-1w levels for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A larger share of time at RESIDENTIAL, paired with suppressed TRANSIT, diverts spending away from in-person retail and delays shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 10 points and TRANSIT remains below its t-0w level across the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility drops more than 15 points week-on-week, leisure substitution weakens and a portion of discretionary outings shifts indoors, increasing RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -48.7 at t-1w to -23.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: After a week-over-week PARKS decline exceeding 15 points, RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -40 for two consecutive weeks, the city is in a restriction-like mobility regime that suppresses discretionary shopping traffic and keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -40 and WORKPLACES below -40 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-four-week mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay below -40 for two full weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL reflects more local errand clustering and home-centered routines; that pattern precedes less nonessential shopping and lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the following week when GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL also remains above zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent trough marks renewed household errand activity and nearby trip generation, which should spill over into more retail visits within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 28 days after GROCERY_PHARM remains less negative than its prior two weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rises while TRANSIT does not recover, warm-weather leisure dominates travel choices and delays indoor shopping, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -50
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days despite PARKS rising and TRANSIT remaining below -50.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES from deeply negative levels signals easing mobility constraints; once both cross upward by at least 10 points from their recent lows, retail and recreation should strengthen over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each rebound by at least 10 points from their recent lows
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved at t-0w versus t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains weaker than the last four-week mean even after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rebound by at least 10 points from their recent lows.
